Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph s. 20?L OPINION NO. 1B SEC. ERNESTO V. PEREZ Director General Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA) 4th and 5th Floor, NFA Building, NFA Compound Attention: MARBIDA L. MARBIDA Better Regulations Office Dear Sec. Perez: This pertains to your letter dated December 04, 2023 on ARTA's endorsement for the conduct of regulatory review on the ordinances of Local Govemment Unit (LGUs) of Taguig City and the Provincial Government of Cavite. This likewise refers to numerous requests for clarifications both ARTA and this department's Bureau of Local Govemment Supervision (BLGS) are receiving particularly on the application of E.O. No. 41 to Section 141 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Govemment Code of 1991". At the outset, we acknowledge and support the need for regulatory review which is based on the requirement of Section 5 of Republic Act No. 11032, or the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Govemment Service Delivery Act of 2018". We confirm that in the case of LGUs, taking account the principle of local autonomy guaranteed by no less than the 1987 Philippine Constitution, this regulatory review is captured by the mechanism set by the Local Govemment Code (LGC) through the approval and review of ordinances and veto power laid down by Sections 54 to 57. Particularly on the review by higher sanggunian of the ordinances and resolutions enacted by component LGUs, the reviewing sanggunian is tasked to check whether the ordinances or resolutions is within the authority of the concemed sanggunian to enact and nothing contained in it was included/passed in an ultra vires capacity, and that the ordinance is consistent with law and other policies. By the peculiar nature of LGUs having local autonomy coupled with the jurisprudentially established doctrine of presumptive validity of legislative enactments, anything beyond the findings of the reviewing sanggunian is a judicial matter cognizable by the proper courts. From this respect, this Department is to remind reviewing sanggunians to take into account compliance to Executive Order No. 41 in its review of component LGUs' ordinances and resolutions. " Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan"

ON THIS DEPARTMENT'S RESPONSIBILITY ON THE REVIEW OF ORDINANCES PURSUANT TO SECTION 2 OF E.O. NO. 41: In order not to violate constitutional restrictions, it is submitted that the nature of review by concerned national agencies as mentioned in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of E.O. No. 41 is limited to consistency or inconsistency with, and applicability of, E.O. No. 41 to a specific imposition being clarified by the requesting LGU. As for this department, that is within the function and mandate of the Policy Compliance Monitoring Division (PCMD) of the Bureau of Local Government Supervision (BLGS). Therefore, that limited aspect of review is still confined with the executive department's implementation and monitoring aspect of LGUs' compliance of E.O. No. 41 aligned with general supervision mandate of the department, and will not be adjudged as an executive over-reach of the functions of the local legislative bodies and the judiciary's power to review its constitutionality. We make clarifications pertaining to the endorsement of ordinances for review by LLLS apparently based on Item 5.1.4 of DILG-ARTA-DOF JMC No. 2021-01 which states that the Legal and Legislative Liaison Service (LLLS) shall cause the validation of all existing local ordinance and verify if any provisions stated therein violate the provisions of the said JMC relative to the imposition of pass-through fees. It is timely to rectify this matter. The validation contemplated therein does not pertain to comprehensive evaluation of validity of an ordinance as it will be tantamount to encroachment of local legislative power and the judiciary's power of judicial review. The limitation of the assailed provision is that those that will be validated by the LLLS are only those endorsed by the BLGS for the issuance of show-cause orders after its initial review and recommendation for the issuance of show-cause orders. This is because the then existing JMC was anchored on an indisputable prohibition on pass-through fees imposition under Section 133 (e) of the LGC. In view of the DILG-ARTA-DOF JMC No.2021-011 having been superseded by the issuance of E.O. No. 41 and its IRR, coupled with the numerous endorsements being forwarded to LLLS for the review of the submitted ordinances relative to Section 141 of the LGC, we hereby resolve to provide herein position/opinion which may serve as guidance for the PCMD, BLGS, in the conduct of review of ordinances for its compliance-monitoring function. I Proper imposition based on Section 141 of the LGC is not covered bv E.O. NO. 41 s. 2023 The imposition sanctioned by Section 141 of the LGC is an Annual Fixed Tax on every delivery vehicle used by manufacturers, producers, wholesalers, dealers or retailers in the delivery of certain commodities. It is readily assessed, imposed and collected once a year by provinces by virtue of Section 141, LGC, and by cities by virtue of Section 141 in relation to Section 151, LGC. It is not an imposition levied every time a vehicle passes through a certain territory, thus, not a pass-through fee imposition. To wit: SEC. 141. Annual Fixed Tax For Every Delivery Truck or Van of Manufacturers or Producers, Wholesalers of, Dealers, or Retailers in, Certain Products. - (a) The province may levy an annual fixed tax for every truck, van or any vehicle used by manufacturers, producers, 1 "OMNIBUS GUIDELINES ON THE SUSPENSION OF LGU IMPOSITION AND COLLECTION OF ILLEGAL FEES AND TAXES RELATIVE TO THE TRANSPORT OF GOODS AND PRODUCTS" Page 2 of 5

wholesalers, dealers or retailers in the delivery or distribution of distilled spirits, fermented liquors, soft drinks, cigars and cigarettes, and other products as may be determined by the sangguniang panlalawigan, to sales outlets, or consumers, whether directly or indirectly, within the province in an amount not exceeding Five hundred pesos (P500.OO). (b) The manufacturers, producers, wholesalers, dealers, and retailers referred to in the immediately foregoing paragraph shall be exempt from the tax on peddlers prescribed elsewhere in this Code. To elaborate further on this position, we provide that the appreciation of Section 141 presupposes the following instances: 1. That the business entity to which the Annual Fixed Tax for every delivery truck or van is imposed has a principal/branch office, sales outlet, plant or warehouse within the territorial jurisdiction of the province imposing said tax; or 2. If there is no such office, sales outlet, plant or warehouse, the province imposing the Annual Final Tax is the point of destination or place of delivery of goods and merchandise transported. Hence, the imposition is clearly not "Pass-Through Fees". The first instance is incidental to being a subject of taxation of the province as a taxing authority following the general rule of situs of local taxation and the second instance being based on the "doing of business" principle. We explain further the importance of having these two instances within the contemplation of Section 141, LGC. On the ISt instance, the provincial treasurer by virtue of said provision can assess outright all business entities with principal/branch office, sales outlet, plant or warehouse in any of its component LGUs for the use of their delivery trucks where the destination or place of delivery is still within the territorial jurisdiction of the province. We bear in mind that the provision classified the amount to be collected as tax, Annual Fixed Tax. Section 166 thereof provides that all local taxes, fees and charges shall accrue on the ISt day of January of each year. Following Section 194 of the LGC, the provincial treasurer can issue the assessment thereon within five (5) years from the date the Annual Fixed Tax became due. Hence, with this interpretation, the provincial LGU is assured of its revenue raising source on the basis of this provision. On the 2nd instance, considering that the point of destination or place of delivery of goods and merchandise is within the territorial jurisdiction of the provincial LGU, there exist "doing business" within the territory which is the rationale of the authority to tax behind Section 141, LGC. By "doing business" we follow the jurisprudential definition which states: (t)he term "doing business" implies a continuitv of commercial dealings and arrangements. and contemplates, to that extent, the performance of acts or works or the exercise of some of the functions normally incident to, and in proqressive prosecution of commercial gain or for purpose of business organization2. The assessment and collection of Annual Fixed Tax in this instance, however, is not outright because the business entity has no office, sales outlet, plant or warehouse and thus no official business address where the tax assessment of the provincial treasurer may be delivered/tendered. It is merely dependent upon enforcement measures of the provincial government and/or upon the application for voluntary assessment by these business entities with regular deliveries to the territorial jurisdiction of the imposing province. 2 BOAC v. commissioner, 149 SCRA 395 or G.R. NO. L-65773-74 April 30, 1987 Page 3 of 5

Having laid the foregoing premise, it is now settled that the imposition of provincial LGUs of Annual Fixed Tax for every delivery truck or van pursuant to Section 141 of the Local Government Code is not within the prohibition provided under E.O. 41 s. 2023. We reiterate, this presupposes that the use of said legal basis and its enforcement are proper. The only exception that we can provide, therefore, is on cases when "Pass-Through Fee" is assessed/imposed/collected "in the quise of" an imposition "apparentlv based" on Section 141, LGC. On the coveraqe of E.O. No. 41 II E.O. 41, on the other hand, covers the following: (a) A prohibition from collecting toll fees and charges upon all motor vehicles transporting goods or merchandise while passing through national roads and such other roads not constructed and funded by LGUs. The prohibition covered by this subsection encompasses the imposition which falls within the prohibition under Section 133 (e) of the LGC but imposed "in the guise of' other fees and charges. This includes those impositions apparently based on Section 155 of the LGC but constitutes pass-through fees contemplated under Section 133 (e) of the LGC. For this purpose, Section 155 is hereinbelow cited: SEC. 155. Toll Fees or Charges. - The sanggunian concerned may prescribe the terms and conditions and fix the rates for the imposition of toll fees or charges for the use of any public road, pier or wharf, waterway, bridge, ferry or telecommunication system funded and constructed by the local government unit concerned: Provided, That no such toll fees or charges shall be collected from officers and enlisted men of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and members of the Philippine National Police on mission, post office personnel delivering mail, physically-handicapped, and disabled citizens who are sixty-five (65) years or older. When public safety and welfare so requires, the sanggunian concerned may discontinue the collection of the tolls, and thereafter the said facility shall be free and open for public use. (b) A strong urge or encouragement for the suspension of imposition/collection of fees, such as but not limited to, sticker fees, discharging fees, delivery fees, market fees, toll fees, or Mayor's Permit fees, that are imposed upon all motor vehicles transporting goods and passing through any local public roads constructed and funded by said LGUs. This includes those impositions of fees and charges anchored on Section 153 of the LGC, to wit: SEC. 153. Service Fees and Charges. - Local government units may impose and collect such reasonable fees and charges for services rendered. In the interim, we extend assistance in the initial evaluation of the ordinances that have already been endorsed to LLLS by providing PCMD, BLGS, with a Compliance- Monitoring Matrix. Moving forward, the concerned bureau, may take consideration of the guidelines provided herein in its fulfillment of the department's responsibilities Page 4 of 5

outlined in Section 2 of the signed E.O. No. 41. Further, it is respectfully recommended that the concerned bureau maintain a database on this in preparation for reports/updates on the implementation of E.O. No. 41 that may be requested by the Office of the President. Finally, the foregoing opinion herein-above discussed is being rendered without prejudice to contrary opinion or ruling that may be issued by competent authorities and/or the proper courts. We hope to have substantially provided the needed assistance. Thank you. Very truly yours, BYTH ATTY. THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: IC .
